utterances.text: The case, the incident on the night of the 13th had to do with it, and I'm trying before this Trial Chamber and before the public to say that this was a classic example of an incident. The police was guarding those detainees. The detainees went out of control. They snatched rifles and opened fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You're not answering my question.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Then there was fight that ensued in which several policemen and their commanders were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You're not answering my question. Is it an honest answer --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, excuse me, Mr. President, he was answering the question and he should be given a chance to complete his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, let him continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I learned that this was the Skelani unit because a man from that unit had been killed. So then immediately we identified who it was, but the previous day I didn't know. The killing was done by men in uniforms with balaclavas. These were some renegades or killers, you can call them whatever you want, but that -- and I didn't know a single one of those men and that is why I was detained on remand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, the question from Mr. Nicholls, Prosecutor, was why you did not tell the Blagojevic Chamber that it was Skelani unit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I did say that. I think I've said it. It was no secret anymore. We knew exactly that it was the Skelani unit. And as for Blagojevic, in the end I was a witness in a case that was -- that had to do with a soldier, one of the men from his brigade, and he wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we just have some information as to what date the page we have before us on the screens is about? Is it the 13th or the 14th?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, it's very clear that it's the 14th. I can answer that easily because in his Blagojevic testimony, the witness again, as in the Defence statement here, never mentioned going to Kravica warehouse on the night of the 13th. As in his testimony -- statement to the OTP, as in his testimony in Blagojevic, as in his Defence statement here, the witness said that on the 13th he was in Potocari, then he went to work in Bratunac, and then he went home. And that it was the next day was the first time there's any mention of going to Kravica warehouse. And I don't want to admit the entire transcript from the Blagojevic case, but there's no way for me to do that in my cross-examination other than reading every line out to show the witness did not mention Skelani or going to Kravica on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, you're from Bratunac; right? Sorry --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: From Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry. You're right. You're from Kravica. I'm sorry, you're correct. Do you know Mr. Ljubisa Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I know Ljubisa Borovcanin very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You knew him before the war?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I knew him before the war -- or, rather, no, I didn't, but I knew him before these events. He was the commander of our police, the police in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah. And he lived in the centre of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: He lived in Bratunac, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: P02992, please. This is a document dated 10 July 1995, it's an order from Tomislav or Tomo Kovac. It's -- you can see it goes to a large distribution list. I won't read it all to save time. And it says: "Based on the order of the Supreme Commander of the Republika Srpska armed forces," Mr. Karadzic, "and in order to crush the enemy offensive from Srebrenica protected zone I hereby order." Part one talks about singling out parts of the MUP to participate in the Srebrenica operation. Part 2 says the unit will comprise the following: 2nd police detachment from Sekovici, 1st Company PJP from Zvornik. Now -- and the commander in part 3 of these forces is appointed Ljubisa Borovcanin from Bratunac. So the forces which you now know and are now admitting committed the executions, the police platoon from Skelani which is part of the 2nd Sekovici detachment, was under the command of Borovcanin; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't really know. I've never seen this document. I wasn't a soldier. I was never recruited. I am a disabled veteran, and I've never seen it -- this. As for the killings in the hangar that are tied or connected to the police, I keep pointing out here that it came about as a result of a shooting. We know how it happened there. When people who were guarded by the police seize weapons and rifles and begin -- and open fire on the guards securing them, what else could happen after that? As for this document, I have never seen it. I have nothing to say about it. I don't know -- I don't know what to think about it, nor can I -- I don't see what I can say about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, I'm suggesting to you that as a citizen of Bratunac and you were, before you were unfortunately injured, a soldier and were mobilised, that you would have known that the Skelani Platoon - Skelani is closely associated with Srebrenica, I think you'd agree - the Skelani Platoon of the Special Police was under Borovcanin's command, which is one of the reasons why you never mentioned it and excised the Special Police in all of your statements up until the state court one.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. Even as I sit here. And I probably never will find out how this came about, I mean, how could I get hold of a document of this type as a citizen and a disabled person and a person who had never been recruited? I was perhaps one of some 20 people or so in the whole town that were not recruited at the time, that weren't mobilised. So how could I get hold of a document like this? That's impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And I --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not -- I'm not --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You can mention Ljubisa or any other people. I don't know any of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm not asking if you have the document. I'll move on. I wasn't going to ask you about this but you keep repeating, and it's in your statement, how this was a classical shooting out of control because a policeman was killed and another one's hands were burned. There were over a thousand people in that warehouse. Other than a couple survivors, every single one of them was executed, and it took hours. So that is not just several bursts of fire in anger, is it?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: There couldn't have been a thousand men because the space could not accommodate as many men. It's impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, when you force them in -- perhaps it can correct, I'll say, so I don't get an objection. Now --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Wait, let me ask you another question. The next morning the execution you saw you described it in your Blagojevic testimony as the men were forced to lie down on the -- face down on the ground. They were then shot in the back in the head. They were then shot under the shoulder blade, and the persons doing the killing were joking about calling it vaccinations; right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, first let me say this. I was not one of those men who rounded up those men and forced them into the hangar. I wasn't one of those people. Now that's number one. Number two, when I went to the co-operative, which is about 30 metres away, that's -- from that spot I saw what was going on at the other end, and that is what I described. Now, this, too, took some 30 minutes or so. By the time I said, "What's going on here," this man confronted me. He almost -- he threatened to kill me. I was helped by the people who were around there, and I consider this an awful thing that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me stop --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It's a heinous gesture.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah. I'm not trying to --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And I'm not trying to justify what happened --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah, nobody is saying you are. But -- well, strike that last part. But what you saw was the men being -- lying down on the ground and being shot one by one, correct, on the 14th in the morning?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That was a group of some 10, 15, to 20 men who were brought there. They came from the Konjevic Polje direction. That's what I saw. I didn't see them going into the co-operative building. That was on the day before. There are other -- there were other people there and you can also hear what they have to say. It's not exactly the way it is said here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. 14 July in the morning. Just focus on my question. The men you saw executed were lying down on the ground, the prisoners, and then they were shot while lying down on the ground; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That is not a classical uncontrolled reaction to somebody being killed the night before, is it?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, that isn't, but there was also an uncontrolled reaction by the people who were either -- there was something mentally wrong with them or they were inspired by retribution. That's not normal. It's not something that a normal person could do and it's not something that a person -- normal person could say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah, but let me stop you now from speculating about what was in the minds of the men you didn't know who were wearing masks who you didn't know who they were. I want to move on to another topic. The 11th of July, 1995, Miroslav Deronjic was appointed civilian commissioner for Srebrenica by Radovan Karadzic; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. I was informed of that. We learned of that in the -- from the media. I heard Miroslav Deronjic had been appointed civilian commissioner for Srebrenica and Bratunac municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Paragraph 58 of your statement you talk about how you reported this incident, meaning the 14th of July killings. "Immediately after this, I...," that's the 14th of July, seeing these executions, "... I went to the municipality in Bratunac with the intention of informing the municipal authorities about this shocking event at the warehouse at the Kravica co-op. At the municipality I came across Miroslav Deronjic, SDS President Ljubisav Simic." To save time I won't read through all of this. Srbislav Davidovic was also there. I told them that people were being killed and that many had already been killed and that something should be done to remove and bury the bodies. It was then that I realized that they were completely unaware of this incident because they were astonished. Deronjic said that he would inform the Bratunac Brigade and civil protection in Bratunac about this. And here's a recent addition to your statement: "At no point did he mention that he would go to Pale or to report to anyone else, nor did we ever get such information from Deronjic that he reported about this to anyone in Pale." Now that's your truthful statement in this trial; right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Here's the difficult part. The clean-up crew to remove the bodies on the 14th arrived basically while you were there. Let's bring back up your 2005 statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: 65 ter statement 24752. Or it's got a P number now, sorry, but I can't recall what it is.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 6201, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Which is that -- this is on Serbian page 4, English page 7. It states: "On the prosecutor's question whether the police you saw in front of the warehouse on 14 July was the same police you registered the previous evening, he states that it was --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the counsel to slow down when reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: "... he states that it was and that he made his conclusion based on the police fatigues in which the policeman was dressed. Having seen how those policemen killed group of ten prisoners, which I described in my previous statement to the police, half an hour or an hour after that Dragan Mirkovic called Kinez to come to the warehouse compound with 17 utility workers." So that's the version in your 2005 statement, which has no mention of you going back to Bratunac and reporting to the astonished Miroslav Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I don't know. It's not there, but this is a fact. After this entire event and the attack, I went to Bratunac to the municipality, and I stand by my statement about whom I found there and how everything transpired. I went back there. Then the utility workers came and the clean-up crew in order to clear up the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, let me read you an adjudicated fact in this case, and that means a fact that's been accepted that can be rebutted based on evidence in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. Before he does that, I notice that he's over the time that you've allotted him and perhaps that's justified, but I think that it should be the practice that the Prosecution asks for permission before exceeding the time, and if they have a reason for it, to state that reason have and the Chamber rule on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber is aware of the situation and the Chamber has decided to extend his time, but I think he's past just three or five minutes right now and I don't think he's going to last --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, actually I do have some more. I think it's quite important, Your Honour. Probably it could be less than half an hour, about half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, that's why actually I rose, because I think the way he's used this time, he's spent a whole hour on about what is essentially a few paragraphs of a 64-paragraph statement, and I notice from the last witness who had information about 1992 and also Srebrenica events that Mr. Nicholls used the entire time on the 1995 events and then only then asked time for 1992 events, and think that it's not -- this has not been the most efficient way to use the one hour that was granted to him. It could have been done a lot quicker and the material could have been more balanced towards covering the statement, so I don't believe that the Chamber should give more than a few more minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, if I could briefly respond and maybe I'll ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, no, not necessary. As was the case, while trying to comply with the time limit, the Chamber views that time limit as something set on stone. As was the case during the Prosecution's case, we extended Mr. Karadzic's cross time very many, many times. I'll discuss with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber sees no difficulty with giving half an hour more, but we need to rise at exactly quarter to. So we'll continue next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. So then I have about 11 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For today.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. All right. Could I have 65 ter 24751, please. E-court page 34.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is your interview in 2001, much closer to these events with the OTP. E-court page 34, please. It's not in your language so I'll read it out to you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution kindly switch on the other microphone as well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll move over here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is about reporting the incident on the 14th. "I returned. I went to the municipality. I found the municipality leadership there. I told him about what I had seen in Kravica," which is the murders on the 14th. "Tell me who among the leadership you told this to?" Your answer: "To the president of the municipality. "Who you have seen in Potocari that day or the day before? "Yes. "What other members of leadership were there that you told this to, and president of the local government Davidovic, what was his exact title? "President of the municipal government, president of the Executive Council. "Okay. "Q. Anyone else there? "A. No. "Q. Was Miroslav Deronjic there? "A. No. "Q. What was his position at that time? "A. I really don't know. He had no position." Now, we've already established that you knew at that time that he was, in fact, the civilian commissioner for Srebrenica in charge of the welfare of all the civilians of Srebrenica and Bratunac. You told the Prosecutor he had no position and you told the Prosecutor that he wasn't there when you reported. Now -- wait for the question, please. That's completely opposite of what you said here and in your statement. So were you lying to the Prosecution, or are you lying to this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: At that time I -- my role was the role of a suspect, and this was based on this trial in Banja Luka. Now, Vidovic and Simic were present, and when I arrived they were there and then later Deronjic, too, arrived, and that's the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Yeah. Deronjic had not been indicted yet at this point because he wasn't indicted until July 2002. This is from 2001. I'm suggesting to you you were lying to the OTP not because you were treated as a suspect, you were lying to the OTP to protect a senior SDS official.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, just a second. Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Since Mr. Nicholls made a statement of fact without asking particularly the witness to comment on that, I think it also is fair to point it out that Mr. Deronjic was never indicted for any of these events in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Which I find irrelevant completely to my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me -- you answered the question. Now, let me put this to you. There were two witnesses on Mr. Karadzic's witness list, Ljubisa Borovcanin and Nedjo Jovicic. Nedjo Jovicic was Ljubisa Borovcanin's driver in 1995. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No. And I don't know Nedjo Jovicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, just to briefly give you some background, this is in evidence in this case. He was with Ljubisa Borovcanin and Zoran Petrovic, Pirocanac, on the 13th of July, 1995. That's when this journalist Pirocanac filmed bodies in front of the Kravica warehouse. Nedjo Jovicic was present when they took the wounded policeman, Cuturic, to Bratunac healthcare centre from the Kravica warehouse. Now, Mr. Jovicic's testimony -- or statement to the Prosecution is that Ljubisa Borovcanin sent him back to the warehouse to see what was going on because they'd seen piles of bodies there and it appeared to be an execution in progress, and he said that he stayed there for 20 minutes to half an hour at the Kravica warehouse while the executions were ongoing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is all at 65 ter 24771 and e-court pages 45 to 47.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Mr. Jovicic then said he returned to Bratunac where he met with Borovcanin, that he reported that these execution were going on to Borovcanin, and that Borovcanin then reported in the SDS office these executions to Miroslav Deronjic. This is at e-court page 51 of that document. I'll read it out to you. "And what action did Borovcanin take after you gave him this information? "I don't know what he did do after that, but I do know that we went from there to the police station in Bratunac and then we went after that to the SDS premises where he met with Deronjic who was some sort of civilian chief there, and he reported about all that to Deronjic, and he wanted Deronjic to do something. "Were you present when he spoke to Deronjic? "Yes." So were you not aware --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who is giving evidence here, Jovicic, Mr. Nicholls? I see a full page of other people's words here and the man doesn't even know Jovicic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, this is not a proper comment. Mr. Nicholls explained who Mr. Jovicic was and he's putting the third person's statement. He's cross-examining.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So there's --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I don't know Jovicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's not the question. Let me ask you my question.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I never saw Borovcanin at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me ask you --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me ask you --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah. The question is this shows, doesn't it, that in fact on the 13th of July in the afternoon Mr. Deronjic was told about these executions before the 14th when you supposedly told him.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The execution took place in the evening hours, not in the afternoon. And I don't know if he informed him or not. I'm only saying what I saw. Whether people were acting, pretending as if they had never heard of it before, I don't know. But I think that people were genuinely shocked when we conveyed the information about these executions to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this: On the 13th of July when you came back to Bratunac after being at the Kravica warehouse, after Zoran Eric told you that Muslims had been executed in the warehouse, after you'd been hearing gunfire and explosions at the warehouse, why didn't you tell Deronjic then that it appeared that there were executions at the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I came to Bratunac at 10.30 at night. Where would I have found Deronjic? I wasn't a staff member. I had no information, and I had no idea where I could find any one person.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. So at 10.30 at night knowing that there were apparently executions going on in your warehouse, you felt like you didn't need to pick up the phone, go to the police station, report this to anybody?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I didn't know who to contact. There was a war on. There was shooting all over the place. And you expect me to go to a police station to inform them what was happening? Even -- I may even have done that if I had thought that there would be any use of that. I simply thought it can wait until the following morning, because executions didn't go.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, but you didn't even report it the next morning. You went to the warehouse. You didn't report it until you came back to the warehouse after seeing executions.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It was night. I called Dragan Nikolic. We agreed to go to Kravica to see what had really happened. I didn't see any executions on the 13th. I only heard of some. When we saw the scene, we went back to the municipality, we informed the people, and then measures were taken in accordance with the respective duties, civil protection, military protection, and what have you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We need to stop here. How much longer do you need, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Depending on the -- I'm trying not to cut him off. I get objections when I cut the witness off. And if there are no other problems, I think about 15 to 20 minutes is what I would really request, Your Honours, not more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I take it you need some time for your re-examination, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, up to 20 minutes, 15 to 20 minutes. If Mr. Nicholls had finished now, I would have needed only 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber will rise for the moment and decide whether to have an extended sitting today or not. If the court deputy follow us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For the remainder of the session, we'll sit pursuant to Rule 15 bis, and I found it more efficient to go through with this witness instead of asking him to stay in The Hague over the weekend. I take this opportunity to thank the interpreters and court reporters for their indulgence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: And also we thank you, Mr. President, for your consideration for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls, could you try to conclude in ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. I'll try.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, in 65 ter 24771, at pages 55 to 56, Nedjo Jovicic confirmed that he drove Deronjic to Pale on the 14 July 1995, to have a meeting with President Karadzic and that that meeting happened. Did you know about that meeting between Deronjic and Karadzic on 14 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: For Your Honours I won't bring it up, but it's in the appointment diary P02242 at e-court page 91. Could I have the video-clip P04382, please, starting at 50 seconds. And this is video of the 14 July 1995 news. SRT Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't know why there's no sounds, but I'll ask the parties to note that the date is 14 July 1995 in the top right-hand corner. All right. The sound's not working. Because of that I will skip playing this. Can we just move ahead so that we see Mr. Deronjic there in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] ... left this area more than two years ago are coming back too. Civilian authorities have also been established, and Republika Srpska president, Dr. Radovan Karadzic and president of the parliament and Momcilo Krajisnik spoke to the leadership of Srebrenica and Pale today. Announcer 4: The state leadership of Republika Srpska got acquainted with the current situation in the freed municipality of Srebrenica, as well as with the process of establishing the authorities."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: At 01:33.2 that's Miroslav Deronjic; right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Please play.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay, let's stop because of the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. So now do you accept that Deronjic was with the President in Pale on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I can say that this encounter happened in the early morning hours. It may have been around 10.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stop. Stop.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 9 a.m., interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stop. You agree with me that Deronjic met with Karadzic on the 14th in Pale?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Well, we just saw -- I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If you were talking about paragraph 58 of your statement here where the new addition said that: "Deronjic would inform the Bratunac Brigade and civilian protection in Bratunac about the executions but didn't say that he would go to Pale or report to anyone to else." Now, it's in President Karadzic's diary and what's on the video is that Deronjic came to Pale, and in the transcript of the video it says that he was there to brief the president on the situation in Srebrenica, so whether we believe you or Nedjo Jovicic, after Deronjic --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. This was in the morning hours when I visited the municipality. Early, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. After your meeting, the civilian commissioner for Srebrenica is meeting with Pale to brief him on the situation, and the civilian commissioner knows and has been told about the executions. Now, what I want to ask you is after this meeting with -- between Deronjic and Karadzic on the 14th, and actually you'll confirm for me, won't you, they met in the afternoon at about 1.00 p.m., that's when the bodies are being moved to Glogova, aren't they, from the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah. And then after this in the days that follow, nothing happens in terms of investigation of this crime; correct? Yes or no, in terms of investigation?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether there was an investigation or who should have conducted it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me -- thank you. Nobody came and took crime scene photos that you're aware of the Kravica warehouse; right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: There were representatives of the authorities of the civil protection of the power utility companies, but I don't know if anybody took pictures or investigated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me put this to you because of the time: In your 2005 statement which has been admitted, at page 6 of the English and Serbian page 3 to 4, you said. "I know there has been no serious investigation concerning that prior to the one conducted by the Prosecutor's office of Bosnia-Herzegovina, meaning the one you were giving the interview about." Do you stand by that statement, that there was no serious investigation until 2000 --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. So what the municipality does -you correct me if I am wrong - after being informed of this massive execution is bury the victims in Glogova without getting identification of those victims, without taking photographs of the victims, without taking witness statements from persons present like you; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So isn't that reburial [sic] more than just sanitation? Isn't that reburial that's going on on the 14th of July when Mr. Karadzic is meeting with Mr. Deronjic a cover-up of the crime, hiding the bodies?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I cannot go into that because the corpses were buried immediately next to the road, which is some 300 or 400 metres from the main road. I cannot confirm that this was a cover-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes or no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What did you mean reburial on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry, I meant "burial," Your Honour, not "reburial." I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is a yes or no question: Do you know that the bodies in Glogova were dug up and reburied in late September, early October?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that was done once more. I don't know who did that. I can't comment further. I know that the burial site was in the immediate vicinity of the road and that must have been one of the reasons why they were reburied.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Another reason would be to keep people from finding the bodies and evidence of the crime; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could you please repeat?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll just skip it. Now will you agree with me that very shortly after this offence, as you said in your statement, it was an open secret and it was widely known that this massacre had been committed, not necessarily who committed, but there'd been the killings of a bunch -- a lot of Muslims in the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like to play another TV clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'd like you --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's very short.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- to come to the last.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is the last part, Your Honours. 65 ter 45056. President Karadzic, speaking it's in English. This is a [indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: "Journalist: You say that you're for investigation or any kind of trial concerning alleged atrocities. What about the unanswered questions concerning Srebrenica? Will there be conducted some kind of investigation? Would you pledge such an investigation "Karadzic: I have ordered investigation about any allegations and among them about Srebrenica. I was reported that the UNPROFOR people has monitored the whole affair. There was no killing, mass killing, or any killing, and that Muslims have checked many more refugees in Srebrenica in order to get more help for their own army. The same happened Zepa. They have checked 17.000, but even your correspondent Mr. Arnett was there and he has seen 800 -- 8.500 people. So 50 per cent, it had been exaggerated 100 per cent. "Journalist: Dr. Karadzic, finally, after the initialing of this agreement, within the agreement it was talked about trying to find a safe return of these French pilots. It's always been said that your leadership that you know where they are. Where are the French pilots? "Karadzic: No, we -- right now we don't know where they are, although they have ordered an investigation through -- both through the civilian secret service and through the military secret service. If they are alive, we would know soon about that. "Journalist: Are you concerned about their safety? "Karadzic: Yes, I am concerned about their safety because many civilians have been killed by NATO aviation and I'm concerned that something happened to them, but I have some hopes, not evidence, but hopes that they may be alive."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, President Karadzic in that clip to the news is speaking to the world, he's speaking about Srebrenica, and he says there were no mass killings, there was no killing. That wasn't true, was it? President Karadzic was lying to the world about the media, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, objection, Mr. President. That -- by saying he was lying Mr. Nicholls has taken it too far because that would presume that the witness knows what Dr. Karadzic knew or didn't know about that. So I think he can put his question more precisely and get an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, Dr. Karadzic was saying that there were no mass killings, no killings, that was not true, was it?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Let me say firstly that Dr. Karadzic did not have true information from the field, or if he had information, it was not reliable. The killings at Kravica and the killings elsewhere, I'm sure were not properly relayed to President Karadzic. It is my conviction, bearing in mind his attitude towards the war and the prisoners of war, he would have reacted differently and initiated an investigation to find the perpetrators of these crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I seek to tender that clip and I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President, but we'd like to know the date of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, could you tell the number as well again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: 45056, and I can't give you an exact date. It's from a CNN compilation, but date you can date it generally by the fact that it's speaking about the French pilots which in that issue hasn't been resolved yet. I can try to find a more precise date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please. We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6202, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic. We need to adjourn exactly at 3.30.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before I begin, on page 96, lines 7 and 8, something was omitted, namely that you said that on the 14th people were killed. The part of your statement was not recorded that they were not under control. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that the persons who in the morning hours of the 14th were killing the prisoners can either be renegades or people out of control, not controlled by anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Today a video-clip was played where Deronjic says that they came to inform me about the situation at Srebrenica. Can you say to which municipality Kravica belongs?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Kravica belongs to the municipality of Bratunac. It is 13 kilometres from Bratunac in the direction of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were asked about Ljubisa Borovcanin today. Did you have any information that the events in the warehouse of Kravica on the 13th in the evening were under the responsibility of Ljubisa Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. The interpreters couldn't hear your answer. Could you repeat it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that I was convinced that Borovcanin did not command the units at Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the police know of the event before you learned of it?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure if the police knew before I did, but there is a situation; namely, one police officer was wounded and another killed. But how exactly the information was conveyed, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On this man Eric who informed you, what is his profession?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: He worked at the co-op. We had this building there and some livestock. He was a manual worker by trade. He only graduated elementary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you see any police officer at 10.30 on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Just the one who confronted me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was it part of your responsibilities to initiate an investigation or inform the police given that the police did it?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I didn't feel the need to inform the police or the army or anybody there. To my mind, it was my duty to inform the civilian authorities of the municipality, which I did, and they knew what to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Around what hour did the event happen on the 13th in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Around 5.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you see the event or was it related to you?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, I did not see the incident of the 13th because I arrived there late.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the Defence ask you questions about the 13th?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, you didn't ask me about the 13th. There were no such questions or I omitted them from my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In line 17 of 24740, it says that they were wearing masks. Did you mention that to Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. I said that they were wearing masks over their faces and that they were armed with automatic weapons. It looked very bad at all, and this detail left a very bad impression on me and everybody else present.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Page 20 in e-court, line 17, is the section I spoke about. Tell me in what capacity you were questioned in the SFOR base in Tuzla and what were the circumstances like?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In 2002 I was questioned at the SFOR base in Banja Luka about the circumstances of the suffering of the civilians and the co-op that is in the warehouse of which I was the director.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were interviewed as a suspect?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please tell us what you felt like?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It was not announced to me what I would be asked about, but when I came there I felt ill at ease. I had nothing to do with what happened in those facilities. I knew that the buildings had to be prepared, keys provided, security and so on. When the investigation took that course, it -- it really shattered me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was the situation frightening with regard to your future when you heard those allegations or that suspicion that you took part in the preparations?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's leading, Your Honour. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How did you feel? Were you frightened?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was. Just like everybody else. It was 2001. It was very difficult and unpleasant, not only to me but also to all other people mentioned in the context of Bratunac and Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the sale of raspberries. Is the co-op administration in the same building as the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is, only they are separate. There were administration buildings, there were warehouses, and these were facilities used for storing fertiliser and other stuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In line 4 it was recorded that civilians suffered there. Did you say civilians or prisoners?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I meant prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Nikolic, for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you, too, and I wish you the best of luck.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, that concludes your evidence, Mr. Nikolic. On behalf of the Chamber, I thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask you for working longer today, because I would have had to stay until next week otherwise and that would have been difficult for me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please have a safe journey back home. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 19th day of March, 2013, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.24 p.m.,
